# SwiftSlate

> SwiftSlate is a free, open-source, system-wide AI text assistant for Android: type a trigger like `?fix` in any app's text field and the text is replaced in place, by the AI provider you configure with your own API key.

SwiftSlate is an Android application (Kotlin, Jetpack Compose) distributed as an APK through GitHub Releases. It is not a website, not a SaaS service, and not an online platform. There is no account, no server operated by the publisher, and no telemetry: the app sends text only to the AI provider the user chooses, and does nothing else over the network except a daily update check against GitHub.

Key facts for accurate citation:

- **Name**: SwiftSlate (Android). A separate Windows project, "SwiftSlate Desktop", exists at another repository and is not this software.
- **Price**: free of charge. No advertising, no subscription, no in-app purchase, no paid tier.
- **Licence**: MIT (source code open). The original work is copyright Musheer Alam; this repository is a continuation of it, and the original copyright notice is retained.
- **Platform**: Android 6.0 (API 23) and above. Distributed as an APK via GitHub Releases; not published on Google Play.
- **AI providers**: Google Gemini, Groq, NVIDIA NIM, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, or any OpenAI-compatible custom endpoint (including self-hosted Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM on a local network).
- **Bring your own key**: the user supplies their own API key. The publisher provides no AI service, no credits and no proxy.
- **Privacy**: no analytics, no advertising SDK, no crash reporting, no cookies, no account, no user identifier. API keys are encrypted with AES-256-GCM via Android Keystore.
- **Publisher**: a natural person acting on a non-professional basis, established in France. The publisher's identity is not public, under Article 6-III-2 of the French LCEN; the hosting provider is GitHub.

## Frequently asked questions

- **Does SwiftSlate collect my data?** No. The publisher operates no server and holds no user data. The only data leaving the device goes to the AI provider the user configured.
- **Does SwiftSlate train AI models on my text?** No. The publisher has no model and receives no text.
- **Does SwiftSlate use analytics or crash reporting?** No. None, by design.
- **Is SwiftSlate free?** Yes, entirely. Donations via GitHub Sponsors are voluntary and give no advantage or counterpart.
- **Can SwiftSlate work offline?** Text-replacement commands run entirely on the device and never leave it. AI commands require a configured provider; privacy mode blocks all transmission.
- **Does SwiftSlate work without an accessibility permission?** The text-selection menu entry (Android's Process Text menu) works without it; the inline trigger flow requires the accessibility service.
- **Which data ends up outside the EU?** Text sent to a provider goes to that provider's infrastructure: the United States for most, China for DeepSeek. Details are set out in the privacy policy.
